50	  session as if the user had just typed it. A global rule contradicting a
51	  project rule is **asked** - one `AskUserQuestion` per clash, before the work

54	  files absent → `rules-orko: none`. From here on, a standing rule the user

60	    `cheap` each set to the **first** slug in this host's column of
61	    `PLATFORMS.md` § Role tiers (Claude Code: `fable` / `opus` / `sonnet`, the
62	    Agent tool's `model` values; codex: `gpt-6-astra/high` / `gpt-6-astra/medium`
63	    / `gpt-6-astra/low`), a model the user named in this session winning over
64	    the column;
65	  - present → keep its models, drop every `down:` line not dated today.
66	  The shape (`host:`, `deep:`, `build:`, `cheap:`, `written:`, `down:` lines) is
67	  `skills/build-jarvis/references/grade.md` § The tiers file. The file is local to
68	  this machine and account: make sure the repo's `.gitignore` carries
69	  `.skillator/*.local.md` (append the line if missing; a repo with no
70	  `.gitignore` gets one with that line). Report `tiers deep=<m> build=<m>
71	  cheap=<m>`, plus `(<m> down)` for any model marked down today. Nothing is
72	  probed: a model that turns out unavailable is marked down by build-jarvis at
73	  dispatch, which retries one tier lower.
74	  On **Claude Code** also check that `build-jarvis`'s `UserPromptSubmit` route
75	  hook is wired (`build-jarvis/references/route-hook.md`); not wired → say so in
76	  one line and offer it, never wire it silently.
77	- **Upstream watch** (F23c, F29) — only in a repo that has
78	  `skills/design-arwen/UPSTREAM.md` (skillator itself); anywhere else skip it
79	  silently, because those tickets belong on skillator's board, not the user's.
80	  Run `sh practice/scripts/upstream-check.sh --daily` (Windows:
81	  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
82	  practice/scripts/upstream-check.ps1 -Daily`). `--daily` makes it a no-op after
83	  the first finished run of the day; the stamp is
84	  `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/skillator/upstream-check.day`, shared by
85	  every worktree. Also run `sh skills/code-yoda/upstream-check.sh --daily`
86	  (Windows: the `.ps1` beside it, `-Daily`) — code-yoda's manifest, same
87	  output shape, its own stamp. Act on the output of both:
88	  - `skipped:` or exit 0: nothing to do.
89	  - each `changed <name> <old>..<new> <url>` line (exit 1, and also exit 2,
90	    because one failed row does not hide another's change): look for an open
91	    (`[ ]` or `[~]`) ticket line in `TICKETS.md` that names both `<name>` and
92	    `<new>`. If there is one, it is already logged. If not, take a number with
93	    `sh practice/scripts/next-id.sh A` and add
94	    `- [ ] A<n> — absorb <name> <old>..<new> into <skill> (<url>)`, `<skill>`
95	    being the one whose manifest reported it (`design-arwen`, or `code-yoda` for
96	    `ponytail`). The procedure is in that skill's `UPSTREAM.md`.
97	  - each `error` line (exit 2): report it in the active-set line as
98	    `upstreams: check failed (<name>)`. Never call a failed check unchanged. No
99	    stamp is written, so the next session retries it.
100	
101	  This is detection and a ticket, never an edit to the skill. Absorbing is a
102	  normal ticket that someone takes on purpose.
103	
104	Then state the active set in **one line** — not a feature tour:
105	
106	```
107	grayskull-power: board 3 open (B2, F7, A1) · codegraph 412 files indexed · code-yoda full · live-friday armed (npm run dev) · watch-cortana armed at 92% · rules-orko: 2 project · 1 global · tiers deep=fable build=opus cheap=sonnet
108	```
109	
110	The banner is printed at the top of the reply, before any of this. It fires
111	**once per session**, on invoke — not on every routed request.
112	
113	---
114	
115	# Persist it for this project (once, then never again)
116	
117	Activation should survive the session and the host. Every one of these CLIs
118	already reads an always-on instruction file from the repo root — that is the
119	carrier, no hook required.
120	
121	On the **first** invoke in a repo, write these four small files and say so in
122	one line. If `.skillator/grayskull.md` already exists, activation is already
123	persisted: skip this whole step silently.
124	
125	**`.skillator/grayskull.md`** — the single source of truth:
126	
127	```markdown
128	# grayskull-power is ON for this project
129	
130	Load and follow `skillator:grayskull-power` for all work here, before
131	anything else. Claude Code: `Skill` tool; Antigravity: `/grayskull-power`;
132	Pi: `/skill:grayskull-power`; Codex/Cursor: read that skill's `SKILL.md`.
133	Print its banner once per session, then route per table.
134	
135	Standing rules:
136	- `TICKETS.md` is the board — `skillator:tickets-zordon` owns it.
137	- Reproduce before fixing; map with `codegraph` first.
138	- Before every commit: regression sweep, then `/code-review`
139	  (`code-review:code-review`) on the staged diff. `skillator:audit-sherlock`
140	  is the whole-app sweep — pre-release, handover, rot — never per-commit,
141	  never inside an implementer.
142	- Staged work runs to the end, no stop between stages. Six stops: a
143	  destructive op, a security-sensitive action, a side effect outside this
144	  worktree (merge, push, publish), the 7-day limit at 90%, a scope-contract
145	  breach, a failed repro. Else log a `Ruling:` in the run file.
146	  `skillator:relay-morpheus` owns `.skillator/run.md`, updated before
147	  dispatch, never after.
148	- One task per fresh implementer, own prompt, no session history —
149	  `skillator:tasks-sentinels` runs that loop. Same-file tasks do not fan out.
150	- Usage watch — before each non-trivial step run
151	  `<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh check`
152	  (Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File
153	  "<SKILL_DIR>/../watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.ps1" -Mode check`).
154	  It prints `HANDOFF NOW` plus an order — follow it. Claude Code's `Stop`
155	  hook does this already; skip it.
156	```
157	
158	Write that block **verbatim**, with exactly one substitution — `<SKILL_DIR>`,
159	which occurs twice (once for `.sh`, once for `.ps1`). Nothing else in the block
160	varies per repo.
161	
162	`<SKILL_DIR>` is the directory that contains grayskull-power's own `SKILL.md`:
163	
164	- **Normally** — the skill is installed outside the repo — write its **absolute**
165	  path, forward slashes, no trailing slash. e.g.
166	  `C:/Users/me/.claude/plugins/skillator/skills/grayskull-power`.
167	- **If that directory is inside the repo being activated** (skillator itself,
168	  dogfooding), write it **relative to the repo root** instead —
169	  `skills/grayskull-power` — so the file stays correct for every clone.
170	
171	Leave the `/../watch-cortana/…` tail exactly as written; do **not** pre-normalise
172	the `/../` away. The check at `practice/scripts/check-grayskull-sync.sh` compares
173	the live `.skillator/grayskull.md` against this block on precisely that rule, so
174	a hand-tidied path reads as drift.
175	
176	The path must resolve to a real `usage-watch.sh`. In any repo that is *not*
177	skillator, a repo-relative `skills/watch-cortana/…` does not exist — that is why
178	the absolute form is the default.
179	
180	Then the three host pointers, **appended** (never overwriting what is there):
181	
182	| File | Read by | Line to append |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
185	| `AGENTS.md` | Codex, Cursor | `Read and follow ./.skillator/grayskull.md before any work in this repo.` |
186	| `GEMINI.md` | Antigravity | `@.skillator/grayskull.md` |
187	
188	Create a file only if it is missing; if it exists, append the line only when it
189	isn't already present. Three near-identical pointers is deliberate — each host
190	reads its own name, and a symlink is not portable to Windows.
191	
192	Deactivating is deleting `.skillator/grayskull.md`; the pointers then resolve to
193	nothing and are harmless. Say that once, don't repeat it.
